name: GPT-4o mini
summary: OpenAI's small, inexpensive multimodal model. The usual default for high-volume routing, classification, and extraction where GPT-4o quality is not required.
strengths: Very low cost per token at high volume
Fast responses suited to interactive use
Reliable structured output and function calling
limitations: Weaker on complex multi-step reasoning than GPT-4o
Requests leave your network — review before sending regulated data
Subject to provider rate limits and deprecation schedules

name: GPT-4o
summary: OpenAI's flagship general multimodal model, accepting text and images. The fallback for work the local models cannot handle well.
strengths: Strong general reasoning, analysis, and writing
Native image understanding
Mature function calling and JSON mode
limitations: Roughly 17x the input cost of GPT-4o mini
Requests leave your network
Latency higher than the mini tier

name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
summary: Google's fast, low-cost model with a very large context window. Well suited to bulk document processing where the whole corpus fits in one prompt.
strengths: Very large context window for whole-document prompts
Low cost relative to the context it accepts
Native multimodal input
limitations: Quality trails the Pro tier on hard reasoning
Requests leave your network
Large prompts still cost real money — watch token spend

name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
summary: The newer Gemini Flash generation — higher quality than 2.5 Flash at a higher price, keeping the very large context window.
strengths: Better reasoning than 2.5 Flash at similar latency
Very large context window retained
Strong multimodal and multilingual coverage
limitations: Roughly 5x the input cost of 2.5 Flash
Requests leave your network
Newer model — behaviour may shift between revisions

name: Claude Haiku 4.5
summary: Anthropic's fast tier. Aimed at high-volume work where latency matters, while keeping the Claude family's instruction-following behaviour.
strengths: Low latency for interactive and batch workloads
Careful instruction following and refusal behaviour
200K context for long documents
limitations: Costlier than GPT-4o mini or Gemini Flash at the same tier
Behind Sonnet and Opus on hard analysis
Requests leave your network

name: Claude Sonnet 5
summary: Anthropic's balanced tier — the usual default for Claude deployments. Strong at long-document analysis, code review, and structured writing.
strengths: Excellent long-document comprehension and code reasoning
Balanced cost against the Opus tier
Consistent, well-structured long-form output
limitations: 3x the input cost of Haiku
Requests leave your network
Verbose by default — prompt for brevity

name: Claude Opus 5
summary: Anthropic's most capable tier. Reserve it for genuinely hard analysis — at 15 USD per million input tokens it is the most expensive option configured here.
strengths: Top-tier reasoning, research, and complex code work
Best quality available through this gateway
Handles ambiguous, open-ended tasks well
limitations: 5x Sonnet and 100x GPT-4o mini on input cost
Highest latency of the configured models
